question: What does the Comfort Club membership include?
html:
What the Comfort Club includes

The materials behind this answer don't list the Comfort Club's specific inclusions, price or visit schedule, so we won't guess at them. Below is what we can say from our data, and how to get the exact terms.

What our data does show

  • Membership is a core growth lever. Our growth plan expects memberships, together with AI answering and booking, to drive about 10-12% organic growth in the first year (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • We serve three trades. As a One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky operator, we cover heating and cooling, plumbing and electrical (Punctual Pros market profile). Whether the plan covers all three trades or only some isn't stated.
  • Many local homes are older. In our nine-county Central PA core, 45-64% of homes were built before 1980 (Punctual Pros market profile). That is where regular maintenance pays off most.
  • Heating fuel varies by county. About 241k core-PA households heat with fuel oil or propane, including 44.5% in Perry and 37.6% in Lebanon (Punctual Pros market profile). Plan terms may differ by system type, but the data doesn't confirm this.

All figures are planning assumptions, not reported counts. The month-0 figure assumes about 0.9% of core owner-occupied homes (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

How to get exact terms

  • Call or book online, and ask for the current Comfort Club terms sheet.
  • Ask which trades are covered (heating and cooling, plumbing, electrical) and how many tune-ups a year are included.
  • Ask about any discounts, priority scheduling and how renewals work.
  • New Jersey customers served from Beachwood should confirm whether terms match Pennsylvania's.

At about 0.9% of owner-occupied homes (est.), membership is the cheapest recurring revenue in the model and the base that steadies technician schedules through the off-season.

Next actions for the operating team

  1. Publish a one-page Comfort Club terms sheet so the assistant can answer from it. It should cover inclusions, price, visit cadence, trades covered and the cancellation process.
  2. Pull the actual active member count and renewal rate from the field-service system. That will replace the 6,500 estimate.
  3. Confirm whether the Pennsylvania and New Jersey plans differ, and document it.
  4. Test whether oil and propane homes in Perry, Lebanon and Berks need a separate maintenance tier.

# What the Comfort Club includes

The materials behind this answer don't list the Comfort Club's specific inclusions, price or visit schedule, so we won't guess at them. Below is what we can say from our data, and how to get the exact terms.

## What our data does show

- **Membership is a core growth lever.** Our growth plan expects memberships, together with AI answering and booking, to drive about 10-12% organic growth in the first year (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
- **We serve three trades.** As a One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky operator, we cover heating and cooling, plumbing and electrical (Punctual Pros market profile). Whether the plan covers all three trades or only some isn't stated.
- **Many local homes are older.** In our nine-county Central PA core, 45-64% of homes were built before 1980 (Punctual Pros market profile). That is where regular maintenance pays off most.
- **Heating fuel varies by county.** About 241k core-PA households heat with fuel oil or propane, including 44.5% in Perry and 37.6% in Lebanon (Punctual Pros market profile). Plan terms may differ by system type, but the data doesn't confirm this.

## Membership base today and planned

| Point in plan | Members (est.) |
|---|---|
| Month 0 (Oct 2026) | 6,500 |
| Month 12 | 11,000 |
| Month 24 | 20,000 |
| Month 36 | 32,000 |

All figures are planning assumptions, not reported counts. The month-0 figure assumes about 0.9% of core owner-occupied homes (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

## How to get exact terms

- Call or book online, and ask for the current Comfort Club terms sheet.
- Ask which trades are covered (heating and cooling, plumbing, electrical) and how many tune-ups a year are included.
- Ask about any discounts, priority scheduling and how renewals work.
- New Jersey customers served from Beachwood should confirm whether terms match Pennsylvania's.

At about 0.9% of owner-occupied homes (est.), membership is the cheapest recurring revenue in the model and the base that steadies technician schedules through the off-season.

## Next actions for the operating team

1. Publish a one-page Comfort Club terms sheet so the assistant can answer from it. It should cover inclusions, price, visit cadence, trades covered and the cancellation process.
2. Pull the actual active member count and renewal rate from the field-service system. That will replace the 6,500 estimate.
3. Confirm whether the Pennsylvania and New Jersey plans differ, and document it.
4. Test whether oil and propane homes in Perry, Lebanon and Berks need a separate maintenance tier.
